mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen steadily for four consecutive weeks (11.6 to 7.9), indicating people are spending progressively less time at home. This freed time typically converts into out-of-home discretionary activity, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks as the residential-time release continues.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined each of the last four weeks from 11.6 to 7.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise (mean next-28-day value <= mean last-28-day value) despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its downward trend for the following four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in TRANSIT below -10 percent signals a disruption to commuting and errand trips that typically precede retail visits. If TRANSIT crosses this threshold, RETAIL_REC should contract over the following week as fewer people pass through stations near shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -10 percent in the latest weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -10.3 at t-1w, the lowest value in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the week immediately following a TRANSIT reading below -10 percent, despite the threshold being crossed.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility rebounded from -9.1 to -3.0 while TRANSIT stabilized near -9 to -10 over the same period. Joint recovery of commuting-adjacent series (workplace attendance returning alongside stabilized transit use) signals restored daily routines that drive lunchtime and after-work retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT changes by less than 1.5 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rebounded from -9.1 to -3.0 while TRANSIT stayed within -9.4 to -10.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES rises sharply and TRANSIT remains stable, indicating the commuting-retail link is broken.

mechanism_narrative: Singapore enters its wetter northeast monsoon transition from September onward, which historically suppresses outdoor activity captured by PARKS. As PARKS mobility trends lower seasonally, associated outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation footfall (open-air malls, hawker centers, outdoor dining) also declines, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS mobility fell back to -1.3 at t-0w after spiking to 2.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks even as PARKS mobility continues its seasonal decline, indicating no seasonal transmission to retail behavior.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has drifted further negative (-5.7 to -7.1) even as overall mobility normalizes, consistent with reduced precautionary stockpiling under a stabilized reopening policy regime. This normalization frees household spending from essential-goods hoarding toward discretionary retail and recreation, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from -5.7 to -7.1 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise despite continued GROCERY_PHARM decline, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses sharply upward indicating renewed stockpiling behavior unrelated to policy normalization.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself dropped from -2.7 to -4.7 in the most recent week after two weeks of improvement. This single-week dip is consistent with short-term noise rather than a structural reversal, so mean-reversion behavior should pull RETAIL_REC back upward within one week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly mean drops by more than 2 points week-on-week after two prior weeks of improvement
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -2.7 at t-1w to -4.7 at t-0w after improving from -6.1 to -2.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues declining or fails to recover in the week following the dip, showing the drop reflects a genuine trend break rather than noise.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of declining RESIDENTIAL time and recovering WORKPLACES attendance together indicates a compounding return to pre-pandemic daily routines: less home-bound time combined with more office presence jointly increases incidental retail and recreation trips (commute-linked shopping, lunch outings), raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.6 to 7.9 while WORKPLACES recovered from -9.1 to -3.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even though both RESIDENTIAL keeps falling and WORKPLACES keeps recovering simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp PARKS spike to 2.3 at t-1w coincides with a likely school holiday or long-weekend period in Singapore, during which families substitute mall and retail visits with outdoor park activities. Under this regime, a surge in PARKS mobility signals near-term substitution away from retail and recreation venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -5.4 to 2.3 at t-1w while RETAIL_REC simultaneously weakened to -4.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises alongside or shortly after a PARKS spike greater than 5 points, indicating no substitution effect between park visits and retail activity.
